statements.note: "Paved or not" makes the prohibition apply to every left shoulder.

statements.text: FACT [?Most] passing is done on the left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left.

flags.note: Generalization with no proportion given.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass on the right WHEN the road is a multi-lane road OR the road is a one-way road OR the driver is overtaking a streetcar OR the driver is overtaking a vehicle turning left

sources.quote: You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

statements.text: FACT passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait for the vehicle in front to move to the right WHEN the driver is in the left most lane AND a slower vehicle is in front of the driver

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT suddenly change lanes and pass on the right WHEN the driver is in the left most lane AND a slower vehicle is in front of the driver BECAUSE the driver in front may realize the driver wants to pass and move to the right at the same time the driver does

sources.quote: Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is driving on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

statements.text: a driver MUST stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on WHEN the driver is at a streetcar stop UNLESS the stop has an area set aside for streetcar passengers

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.
a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar

statements.note: The passage calls the instruction a rule, giving it legal force.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass an area set aside for streetcar passengers at a [?reasonable] speed AND be prepared for pedestrians to make [?sudden or unexpected] moves WHEN the driver is passing the area

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.
This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

flags.note: No speed measure is given.
No measure of suddenness or unexpectedness is given.

statements.note: "These areas" are resolved as the set-aside streetcar passenger areas from m63.
